item.title: Warm Music for Morning Tips

turns.text: Add some warm, hopeful music to this clip, nothing too energetic. Keep the whole video and my voice.

item.tests: Tests whether the delivered video adds music matching an explicit mood while preserving the source footage and speech.

answer_sheet.Music mood: Warm and hopeful, with gentle energy rather than a driving beat.
answer_sheet.Footage and length: Use the entire attached 10-second clip without changing its visuals or timing.
answer_sheet.Original audio: Keep my original voice audible and understandable.
answer_sheet.Platform, framing, and added text: Keep the original framing. No added text; no particular platform.

must_haves: The output contains the full original 8-second kitchen-table video, with no new shots or altered playback speed.
Added music is clearly audible and has a warm, hopeful, gentle character rather than an aggressive or high-energy feel.
The woman's original spoken introduction remains audible and understandable throughout.
The added music ends with the video rather than continuing over extra footage or a blank screen.
After the follow-up, the final result is about 8 seconds long (the user asked for 2 seconds less); everything else is as before.

changed_by.say: actually, make it 2 seconds shorter and keep everything else the same.

turns.text: Add some warm, hopeful music to this clip, nothing too energetic. Keep the whole video and my voice.

dialog.agent:
I’d use a gentle instrumental bed—soft piano, warm ambient pads, and no strong beat—kept low beneath your voice.

The connected tools can generate music, but they don’t offer a way to mix it into your clip while preserving the **entire video and your original voice**. I won’t regenerate the clip and risk changing either.

To finish it in a video editor, add the music as a separate track, lower it beneath the speech, and fade it in and out. If you tell me the clip’s duration, I can help prepare a matching soundtrack.
dialog.user: Please go ahead with the free settings anyway.

dialog.agent:
Free settings don’t remove the limitation: the connected tools can’t mix background music into your clip while keeping the full video and original voice unchanged.

I can generate a separate gentle, hopeful instrumental track, but I need the **clip’s duration** to match it. You’d then add it as a quiet background track in a video editor. How long is the clip?

The music generator’s minimum length is **15 seconds**, so it can’t make an exact 10-second track. Shall I generate a gentle, hopeful **15-second instrumental** that you can trim to 10 seconds? It will be a separate audio file, not mixed into your video.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the generation because your account has **insufficient credits**. No music was created, and your video is unchanged.

For a royalty-free alternative, look for “gentle hopeful piano ambient”—instrumental, slow, and without drums. Trim it to 10 seconds, keep it low beneath your voice, and add short fades at both ends.

Establish the mood immediately and keep the first 10 seconds musically self-contained and easy to trim, with a soft natural ending for the full 15-second track.
